CFML Language Reference: Functions

StructNew

Returns a new structure with no keys. A structure stores values under names (keys), like a small dictionary.

Category

Structure functions

Syntax

StructNew()

Returns

A new, empty structure.

Usage

Add keys with dot notation (<CFSET s.Name = "Ann">), bracket notation (<CFSET s["Full Name"] = "Ann">) or StructInsert. Key names are not case-sensitive.

Structures are passed by reference: after <CFSET B = A> both names refer to the same structure. Use StructCopy or Duplicate to get a real copy. Literal syntax like {name="Ann"} is from a later century; in 4.5 you always start with StructNew.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Visitor = StructNew()>
<CFSET Visitor.Name = "Pat">
<CFSET Visitor.Browser = "Netscape 4.7">
<CFSET Visitor["Favorite Site"] = "www.gibson.example">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>IsStruct(Visitor) = #IsStruct(Visitor)#, #StructCount(Visitor)# keys.</P>
<UL>
<CFLOOP COLLECTION="#Visitor#" ITEM="Key">
  <LI><B>#Key#</B>: #Visitor[Key]#
</CFLOOP>
</UL>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

StructInsert, IsStruct, StructCopy, Duplicate, ArrayNew
